protocol:
1. Set up the reaction workspace with a blue ice bucket filled with crushed ice, labeled microcentrifuge tubes, a white PCR tube rack, adjustable micropipettes, universal pipette tips, reagent boxes, and a lab notebook.

2. Attach a disposable pipette tip to an adjustable micropipette and set the pipette to the visible 20 µL setting.

3. Open an orange-labeled microcentrifuge tube held on ice, aspirate reagent with the micropipette, and keep the tube cold in the ice bucket.

4. Open a green-labeled microcentrifuge tube held on ice, aspirate reagent with the micropipette, close the tube, and return it to the crushed ice.

5. Open a pink pipette-tip box and load a fresh disposable tip onto a small-volume micropipette.

6. Open a reagent storage box containing multiple labeled microcentrifuge tubes and select a white-capped reagent tube.

7. Open the selected white-capped reagent tube, aspirate reagent with the small-volume micropipette, and add the aliquot to a labeled tube in the white PCR tube rack.

8. Close the reagent tube after pipetting and place it back in the reagent box or rack.

9. Select another labeled white-capped reagent tube from the reagent storage box and open it at the bench.

10. Aspirate reagent from the opened tube with a fresh pipette tip and add the aliquot to the reaction tube in the PCR tube rack.

11. Close the reagent storage box and move the white box labeled for restriction enzymes into the working area.

12. Remove a yellow-labeled enzyme/reagent tube from the white restriction-enzyme box and inspect the tube label before use.

13. Consult the handwritten lab notebook to check the reaction setup and listed reagent volumes.

14. Adjust the micropipette volume using the dial on the handle before pipetting the next reagent.

15. Open the yellow-labeled reagent tube, aspirate reagent with a fresh pipette tip, close the tube, and keep the reagent cold.

16. Open a clear square bottle containing liquid reagent, insert the pipette tip into the bottle, and aspirate liquid into the micropipette.

17. Close the clear reagent bottle with its white cap after removing the aliquot.

18. Add the liquid aliquot from the micropipette to the labeled reaction tube in the white PCR tube rack while maintaining the remaining reaction tubes on ice.
